title.en: China’s Natural Wonders: How Were They Made?
title.zh: 中国的自然奇观：它们是怎样形成的

clips.send: Dunhuang Yardang, Gansu. Gansu, old lake-bed layers, wind-carved ridges. Long ridges shaped like upside-down boats or a fleet of ships, all pointing the same way — the way the wind blows. Yardang comes from a Uyghur word for a steep ridge. Locals call such places “devil city” (魔鬼城) because the wind howls through them. The rock is layers of mud and sand from an old lake. Wind-blown sand works like a sandblaster on the softer layers. Dry lake + strong wind + sand equals yardang.

clips.send: Zhangye Danxia, Gansu. Gansu, red sandstone and mudstone, Danxia (red beds). Hills striped red, orange, yellow and white — the “rainbow mountains”. Danxia (丹霞 dānxiá) means “rosy clouds”. The landform is named after Danxia Mountain in Guangdong, where red cliffs were first described. The colours come from minerals, mostly iron: rusty iron oxide is red, other minerals are yellow, white or grey-green. Red beds + uplift + erosion equals Danxia.

clips.send: Stone Forest (Shilin), Yunnan. Yunnan, limestone, karst stone forest. A “forest” of grey limestone blades and pinnacles, packed so tightly that paths squeeze between them like a maze. Some pinnacles are taller than a 7-storey building. Same rock as Guilin, but here the water cut mostly along close-set vertical cracks, so you get blades instead of big towers. Close cracks, a crowd of stone blades.

clips.send: Mount Huangshan, Anhui. Anhui, granite, peaks and odd rocks. Famous for its “four wonders”: odd-shaped pines, strange rocks, a sea of clouds and hot springs. The highest peak, Lotus Peak, is about 1,865 m (6,100 ft). Granite starts as magma that cools slowly deep underground — the slow cooling grows big crystals you can see. Cracks (joints) cut the granite into blocks; weathering along them makes the sharp peaks and balanced boulders. Cooled underground, lifted up, carved along cracks.

clips.send: Zhangjiajie (Wulingyuan), Hunan. Hunan, quartz sandstone, peak forest. More than 3,000 sandstone pillars, many over 200 m (650 ft) tall — like a forest of 60-storey skyscrapers with pine trees on the roof. The rock is quartz sandstone, which water can’t dissolve. Instead, flowing water, frost and gravity pried it apart along vertical cracks. One pillar was renamed “Avatar Hallelujah Mountain” after the film’s floating mountains. Sandstone + uplift + cracks + water equals pillars.

clips.send: Guilin landscapes (Li River). Guangxi, limestone, karst peak forest. Hundreds of steep limestone towers rise straight out of flat rice fields, with the Li River (漓江 Lí Jiāng) winding between them. Inside, the hills are full of caves such as Reed Flute Cave (芦笛岩) — water has been eating the rock from within, too. The scene is printed on the back of China’s 20-yuan banknote. Limestone + rain + time equals towers and caves.

clips.send: Jiuzhaigou and Huanglong, Sichuan. Sichuan, travertine (calcium carbonate), lakes and pools. Clear turquoise lakes and thousands of terraced pools, rimmed by creamy rock dams. The dams are travertine (钙华 gàihuá): calcium carbonate dropped by water — the same stuff as the white crust in a kettle. In August 2017 an earthquake in Jiuzhaigou broke the dam of Sparkling Lake (火花海) and damaged Nuorilang Falls; both were repaired and the park reopened. Dissolve underground, drop it at the surface.

clips.send: Qomolangma (Mount Everest). Xizang (Tibet), China–Nepal border, 8,848.86 m. The world’s highest peak: 8,848.86 m (29,032 ft), measured jointly by China and Nepal in 2020. That’s about 20 Empire State Buildings stacked up. The rock near the summit is limestone with fossils of sea creatures — it was once the floor of an ocean. The Indian Plate is still pushing north into the Eurasian Plate, so the Himalayas are still rising by a few millimetres a year. Plates collide, sea floor climbs to the sky.

clips.send: 甘肃敦煌雅丹。甘肃 · 古湖泊沉积层 · 风蚀垄岗。一条条长长的土丘像倒扣的船，又像一支舰队，全都朝着同一个方向——风吹来的方向。“雅丹”来自维吾尔语，意思是“陡壁的小丘”。风吹过时呼啸作响，人们称之为“魔鬼城”。岩层是古代湖泊沉积的泥沙。大风挟带的沙粒像“喷砂机”一样，专门打磨松软的岩层。干湖床，大风吹，沙打磨，成雅丹。

clips.send: 四川九寨沟、黄龙。四川 · 钙华 · 彩池与湖泊。湖水清澈碧蓝，成千上万的彩池层层叠叠，被乳白色的钙华堤围起来。这些堤坝是钙华——水中析出的碳酸钙，和水壶里的白色水垢是同一种物质。2017 年 8 月九寨沟发生地震，火花海的钙华堤被冲垮，诺日朗瀑布受损；经过修复，景区已重新开放。地下溶解，出地表沉积。

clips.send: 云南石林。云南 · 石灰岩 · 喀斯特石林。灰色的石灰岩石峰、石柱密密麻麻地排列，像一片“石头森林”，小路在石林间曲折穿行。有的石柱比七层楼还高。和桂林一样是石灰岩，但这里流水主要沿着密集的垂直裂隙溶蚀，所以形成的是一片片石柱，而不是大山峰。裂隙密，石柱林立成石林。

clips.send: 甘肃张掖丹霞。甘肃 · 红色砂岩和泥岩 · 丹霞地貌。山坡上红、橙、黄、白相间，像彩虹一样，被称为“彩色丘陵”。“丹霞”的意思是红色的云霞。这种地貌以广东丹霞山命名。颜色来自岩石中的矿物，主要是铁：氧化铁呈红色，其他矿物呈黄、白、灰绿等颜色。红层抬升遭侵蚀，赤壁丹崖成丹霞。

clips.send: 安徽黄山。安徽 · 花岗岩 · 奇峰怪石。黄山以奇松、怪石、云海、温泉“四绝”闻名，最高峰莲花峰海拔约 1865 米。花岗岩是岩浆在地下深处慢慢冷凝形成的，冷却得慢，所以晶体颗粒大，肉眼可见。节理把花岗岩切割成块，风化和侵蚀沿节理进行，形成陡峭的山峰和奇特的石头。地下冷凝，抬升出露，沿节理雕琢。

clips.send: 珠穆朗玛峰。西藏，中尼边界 · 海拔 8848.86 米。世界最高峰，2020 年中尼两国共同测定海拔 8848.86 米。峰顶附近的岩石是含有海洋生物化石的石灰岩——这里曾经是海底。印度洋板块仍在向北挤压亚欧板块，喜马拉雅山脉至今仍在以每年几毫米的速度升高。板块碰撞挤压，海底升上天。

clips.send: 湖南张家界（武陵源）。湖南 · 石英砂岩 · 峰林。这里有 3000 多座石英砂岩石柱，许多高达 200 米以上，像一片顶上长着松树的“摩天大楼森林”。石英砂岩几乎不溶于水。流水、冻融和重力沿着垂直节理一点点侵蚀、崩塌，才形成石柱。其中一座石峰因电影《阿凡达》中的“悬浮山”而得名“阿凡达-哈利路亚山”。砂岩抬升节理多，流水冻融成峰林。

clips.send: 桂林山水（漓江）。广西 · 石灰岩 · 喀斯特峰林。一座座陡峭的石灰岩山峰拔地而起，漓江在峰林间蜿蜒流过。山体内部有芦笛岩等许多溶洞——流水也在从里面“掏空”岩石。桂林山水的景色印在第五套人民币 20 元纸币的背面。石灰岩 + 雨水 + 时间 等于 峰林和溶洞。
